title: AgentLeak: privacy-leakage testing for agentic AI systems
description: AgentLeak audits complete AI-agent execution traces for privacy leakage across eight instrumented channels (user input, tool responses and calls, shared memory, inter-agent messages, logs, generated files, final output), scores disclosures with AgentRisk, reconstructs source-to-target provenance and enforces release policies through an SDK, CLI, web workspace, MCP server, GitHub Action and sampled monitor. Version 0.20.0 adds AgentSocialBench- and MCPTox-derived scenario packs (491 bundled scenarios), a mapping to OWASP Agentic, MITRE ATLAS and NIST AI 100-2 terms, finding triage in the web workspace, import of promptfoo, Inspect AI, garak and PyRIT outputs, SARIF for traces, and context rules that raise recall on cued prose; it changes some scores, as listed in its changelog. Version 0.19.1 is a security release: it stops a request from choosing which server environment variable the LLM judge reads and where it sends it, and closes the other defects found in a review of 0.19.0. Version 0.19.0 added a research workflow (agentleak bench), an agent self-test (agentleak selftest), check-digit validated identifiers, provider token rules, an InjecAgent-derived scenario pack and security fixes; it changes some scores, as listed in its changelog. Version 0.18.0 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23935443) is the version described and evaluated in the revised SoftwareX article.
notes: Release 0.20.0. Bundled PrivacyLens-derived and MCPTox-derived fixtures are CC BY 4.0, AgentDojo-, InjecAgent- and AgentSocialBench-derived fixtures MIT, with per-pack provenance; AgentLeak-authored code is MIT.
